title: Nuclear mass calculation based on anisotropic kernel ridge regression and $α$-decay chain recursion
summary: Many short-lived or rarely produced nuclei defy direct mass spectrometry, but their masses are constrained by the $α$-decay energies connecting them through decay chains. We combine anisotropic kernel ridge regression (AKRR), an extended Garvey--Kelson relation (GK16), and $α$-decay chain recursion: AKRR learns the residuals between experimental $α$-decay energies and WS4 predictions, GK16 removes residual local fluctuations, and the corrected energies convert a measured anchor mass into the target mass by exact recursion---replacing absolute-mass extrapolation with interpolation of relative decay energies plus exact algebra. The only data-adjusted quantities are the three kernel hyperparameters, fixed by leave-one-out cross validation. For the 22 nuclei whose masses were measured only after AME2003, the $Q_α$ RMSD falls from 169~keV (WS4) to 108~keV (AKRR) and 65~keV (AKRR+GK16), and the mass-excess RMSD reaches 86~keV, versus 348 and 211~keV for WS4 and AKRR. Mass excesses are further predicted for the 122 nuclei with measured $Q_α$ but no directly measured masses.

title: A Predictive Nuclear Effective Field Theory from Wilsonian Renormalization Group Principles I: Medium-mass nuclei and nuclear matter
summary: The predictive power of nuclear effective field theory (EFT) from few- to many-body systems is substantially restricted by regulator dependence. Wilsonian momentum-shell renormalization group (RG) offers a natural framework for cutoff-independent predictions, but its many-body implementation requires regulating single-particle momentum modes, which breaks Galilean invariance. RG scaling analysis shows that this symmetry breaking is encoded in irrelevant operators whose effects can be included explicitly or absorbed into higher-body interactions. Guided by Wilsonian RG, we construct a regularization scheme for chiral EFT contact interactions and predict binding energies of nuclei up to $^{40}$Ca using interactions calibrated only to $A\leq3$ systems. The predicted energies vary at the percent level and agree with experiment for $300\leqΛ\leq450$~MeV. The same scheme reduces the overbinding of symmetric nuclear matter obtained with conventional relative-momentum regulators. Our results suggest that some model dependence observed in nonrelativistic many-body calculations originates from treating EFT vertices as static, Galilean-invariant potentials rather than as field operators regulated consistently across particle-number sectors.

title: A Predictive Nuclear Effective Field Theory from Wilsonian Renormalization Group Principles II: Hidden unitary transformations
summary: A fundamental challenge in nuclear effective field theories (EFTs) is to demonstrate the equivalence of interactions built at different momentum cutoffs and calibrated to the same set of low-momentum observables. Focusing on contact terms, we explicitly construct the unitary transformation that connects these EFT Hamiltonians. By replacing the conventional \emph{relative}-momentum cutoff with a universal single-particle \emph{absolute}-momentum cutoff, we show that this transformation can be systematically implemented using the similarity renormalization group (SRG) technique. The key insight is that such a regularization scheme enables a manifest decoupling of the many-body Fock space, avoiding transitions of particles in intermediate states into high-momentum subspaces associated with conventional \emph{relative}-momentum regulators. The derivation closely parallels the momentum-shell integration formalism of the Wilsonian RG flow. Reformulating the path integral in terms of unitary transformations allows a more intuitive, energy-independent analysis of nonrelativistic many-body systems within the EFT framework. In particular, this framework ensures that effective interactions calibrated in few-body sectors remain unitarily equivalent when applied to many-body systems, a central requirement not yet fulfilled in nuclear many-body calculations. We also show that the breaking of Galilean invariance due to the \emph{absolute}-momentum regularization induces irrelevant operators controlled by the RG scaling behavior, without introducing further complications. We numerically demonstrate our theoretical analysis using a one-dimensional toy model of bosons. These results provide a useful tool for analyzing the RG evolution of nonrelativistic many-body systems.

title: Strangeness-to-entropy ratio across the QCD crossover
summary: We study the absolute open-strangeness density $n_{|S|}$ of strongly interacting matter at vanishing conserved-charge chemical potentials. Unlike the net-strangeness susceptibility $χ_2^S$, this quantity is not a derivative of the QCD partition function and requires a microscopic specification of the strangeness carriers. We use an equation of state that interpolates between an interacting hadron resonance gas and a quark-gluon plasma, with parameters fixed previously by lattice-QCD bulk thermodynamics. The ratio of $n_{|S|}$ to the entropy density $s$ follows the hadron-gas behavior below $T\simeq120$ MeV, rises above the ideal massless $2+1$-flavor limit of approximately $0.053$ across the crossover, and approaches this limit from above at high temperature. The same equation of state, minimally extended to finite $μ_S$, captures the temperature dependence of the lattice-QCD $χ_2^S$. For uncorrelated singly-strange Boltzmann particles, the strangeness fluctuation factor $F_S=χ_2^S/(n_{|S|}/T^3)$ equals unity. Within the constructed equation of state, it deviates from unity by less than $10\%$. This allows us to estimate $n_{|S|}/s$ from lattice-QCD data on $χ_2^S$ and $s$. The lattice-based estimate reaches a maximum of $n_{|S|}/s\simeq0.063$ at $T\simeq220$ MeV, followed by a $20\%$ decrease towards the high-temperature limit.

title: Precision Muon Physics
comment: 30 pages, 11 figures, contribution prepared for Encyclopedia of Nuclear Physics by Elsevier
summary: The muon has become a versatile tool for fundamental physics. Measurements of muon decay determine the Fermi constant and establish the chiral structure of weak interactions. Measurements with stored muons and bound muons enable precision determinations of the muon charge, mass, and magnetic moment. These studies also provide far-reaching tests of bound-state QED and the Standard Model, as well as unique sensitivity to physics beyond our current understanding of the particles, forces, and laws of nature. We survey the landscape of precision muon physics, emphasizing both the physics reach and the experimental breadth. We highlight the range of techniques, from charged-particle timing, tracking, and polarimetry to storage-ring experiments, microwave resonance methods, and Doppler-free laser spectroscopy. We also describe the interplay between experimental work and theoretical developments in quantum electrodynamics, quantum chromodynamics, and effective field theory.

title: Flavor-dependent quark-mass scaling and the fate of the strange-matter window in self-bound quark stars
summary: In the flavor-dependent QMDD model, self-bound $ud$ quark matter can be the ground state at vanishing pressure and convert into $uds$ matter through a first-order transition. So far the mass functional has used parameters $(a,C)$ common to all flavors; here we let the strange sector have its own coupling, $C_s=α\,C_{u,d}$, and map the response of the zero-pressure parameter space. The $e^0_{ud}=930\,$MeV boundary is independent of $α$ by construction, whereas increasing $α$ enlarges the self-bound $ud$ domain and pushes the $e^0_{ud}=e^0_{uds}$ line towards larger $a$. The causality boundary $c^0_s=c$ is almost frozen near $a\simeq5.5$. The competition closes the strange-matter window at \RA{$α_{\rm crit}\simeq1.136$}: above it every causal self-bound parametrization is $ud$ at zero pressure, so a first-order $ud\!\to\!uds$ transition must occur at higher pressure, though not necessarily inside a star, since the maximum mass may be reached below the transition density. The transition pressure and the energy-density jump grow monotonically with $α$, both scale \RB{approximately} with the available-volume fraction $q=1-κ$, and the Seidov onset-instability diagnostic stays below unity.
